Notes on the two lowest-confidence calls, for whoever reviews this batch:
- `f_507ec3f05dc8` ("aliases: Hosted build platform") — the span uses "a hosted build platform" as a common-noun requirement description (lowercase, indefinite article), not as a defined name/alias. Contrast with `f_2cc858f9cb26`, where "package name" appears as the sentence subject in a definitional sentence — that reads as genuine term usage, so I entailed it.
- `f_3e64767d8a79` ("It is integrity threat F") — SLSA's real threats table does classify each lettered threat as integrity/availability, but neither the presented span nor window contains that word, so per the rule ("window is evidence only for distinguishing dropped-vs-fabricated, never for entailing on its own strength") this is fabrication as presented, even though it may be documentably true elsewhere in the source.
